Subtitle: Free • Offline • Privacy friendly
HistoryHint: Long-term history is stored locally at most once every 5 minutes while the app is running.
SummaryExcellent: Capacity is close to the battery's original design capacity.
SummaryGood: Capacity remains healthy for normal use.
SummaryFair: The battery has noticeable capacity wear but can still be usable.
SummaryPoor: Capacity loss is substantial. Runtime may be significantly shorter than when new.
SummaryReplaceSoon: Capacity is heavily degraded. Consider replacement if runtime or stability is no longer acceptable.
SummaryCapacityUnavailable: This laptop did not expose enough capacity data to calculate battery health.
FindingCapacityGoodDetail: Full-charge capacity is about {health}% of design capacity.
FindingCapacityWearDetail: Full-charge capacity is about {health}% of design capacity.
FindingCapacityPoorDetail: Only about {health}% of design capacity remains at full charge.
FindingCapacityCriticalDetail: Only about {health}% of design capacity remains at full charge.
FindingLimitedDataDetail: Some laptop firmware does not expose design or full-charge capacity through Windows.
FindingCycleDetail: The battery reports {cycles} charge/discharge cycles. This value is informational and is not used alone to judge replacement.
FindingCycleUnavailableDetail: The battery or firmware does not report a cycle counter.
FindingVoltageDetail: Current reported battery voltage is {voltage} V. Live Monitor tracks how it changes over time.
FindingVoltageUnavailableDetail: This device does not currently expose battery voltage to the app.
FindingCriticalDetail: The battery driver currently marks the battery state as critical.
LiveMonitorHint: Battery Doctor samples the battery every 5 seconds. Runtime estimates use moving averages to reduce short-lived CPU or browser spikes.
PowerTrendHint: Above zero = charging, below zero = discharging. The chart is observation data, not a cell-level diagnosis.
NoAnomaliesDetail: No sudden percentage drop or large short-term voltage movement was detected in the current live window.
BatteryTestHint: Unplug the charger, start the test, and use the laptop normally for 15–30 minutes. The app records percentage, voltage, and discharge power. Stop if the laptop becomes unusually hot, unstable, or the battery swells.
TestReady: Ready. Unplug the charger before starting.
TestRunning: Test running — keep the charger unplugged.
TestNeedUnplug: The battery is not currently discharging. Unplug the charger, wait a few seconds, then start again.
TestPausedPluggedIn: Test paused because external power is connected. Unplug to continue.
TestComplete: Test complete. Review the graph and observations below.
NoTestAnomaliesDetail: The recorded samples have not shown a sudden percentage drop or a large short-term voltage movement.
TrendHint: Battery Doctor stores a long-term sample about every 5 minutes while running. Existing Phase 1 history remains in the same local database.
AnomalySuddenDropDetail: Charge fell by about {value} percentage points within roughly 90 seconds while discharging. This is a symptom worth repeating in a controlled test; it does not by itself prove a failed cell.
AnomalyVoltageSwingDetail: Reported battery voltage moved by about {value} V within the recent window. Load changes can cause voltage movement, so compare this with charge percentage and power draw before concluding there is a battery fault.
AnomalyPowerSpikeDetail: Discharge power briefly reached about {value} W, much higher than the recent median. This may simply reflect CPU/GPU workload.
HealthCurrentReading: Current firmware/BMS capacity estimate; this is not a direct cell measurement.
RuntimeSource5Minute: Based on the recent moving average (up to 5 min)
RuntimeSourceInstant: Instant estimate; it will stabilize after more samples
RuntimeUnavailable: Not enough power data to estimate runtime
PowerDataPluggedIn: Adapter connected — unplug to measure discharge power
PowerRateUnavailable: Discharging, but this firmware is not reporting power rate
ChargeRateUnavailable: Charging, but this firmware is not reporting charge rate
TestVerdictProvisional: Provisional while the test is running
TestVerdictFinal: Final assessment for this test session
TestVerdictPendingDetail: Start a discharge test to evaluate short-term battery stability.
TestVerdict_insufficient_Detail: The test has run for less than about one minute. Continue testing before interpreting stability.
TestVerdict_short_Title: Short test — no major issue detected so far
TestVerdict_short_Detail: The test lasted about {minutes} minutes. No major sudden-drop symptom was detected, but 15–30 minutes gives a more useful stability check.
TestVerdict_anomaly_Title: A notable discharge anomaly was detected
TestVerdict_anomaly_Detail: The test detected a sudden battery-percentage drop or another high-severity symptom. Repeat the test under a steady workload before drawing a hardware conclusion.
TestVerdict_caution_Title: Discharge was mostly usable, with a stability warning
TestVerdict_caution_Detail: A voltage movement or similar warning was observed. Workload changes can cause this, so repeat the test and compare the same symptom across sessions.
TestVerdict_capacity_worn_stable_Title: Capacity is heavily worn, but short-term discharge looks stable
TestVerdict_capacity_worn_stable_Detail: Battery capacity is about {health}% of design capacity. During this test no major sudden-drop symptom was detected; capacity wear and discharge stability are separate conditions.
TestVerdict_stable_Detail: This test did not detect a major sudden percentage drop or short-term voltage warning. This does not prove every cell is healthy, but the observed discharge was stable.
ExportNotYet: Finish a test to export an HTML + JSON report.
ReportDisclaimer: Battery Doctor reports data exposed by Windows and laptop firmware. Health and test assessments are estimates for maintenance guidance, not a cell-level laboratory diagnosis.
TestAutoComplete: Target duration reached — test completed automatically.
TestProfile_quick_Hint: A short check for obvious percentage drops or voltage instability. Confidence is intentionally limited.
TestProfile_standard_Hint: Recommended general test. Long enough to evaluate runtime, energy agreement, and common gauge problems.
TestProfile_deep_Hint: A longer test for intermittent instability and better usable-capacity estimation.
TestProfile_collapse_Hint: Use this when the laptop reports plenty of charge but suddenly powers off. Keep important work closed; the test continues until you stop it or power is lost.
CollapseJournalHint: During a test, samples are written and flushed to disk every ~2 seconds so an unexpected shutdown can be analyzed after Windows starts again.
RecoveredCollapseHighTitle: Strong sudden-collapse evidence recovered after restart
RecoveredCollapsePossibleTitle: Interrupted discharge test recovered after system restart
RecoveredCollapseHighDetail: Before the restart, Battery Doctor last recorded {last}; after restart Windows reported {current}. About {energy} Wh was delivered before power loss while the firmware still reported about {remaining} Wh remaining. Observed delivered energy in this session was {observed}% of design capacity. This is strong evidence of a gauge/cutoff reliability problem, but it does not identify an individual failed cell.
RecoveredCollapsePossibleDetail: The previous discharge test ended without a clean stop and Windows restarted while the test was active. The last saved charge was {last}; current charge is {current}; about {energy} Wh was recorded. This is possible sudden-collapse evidence, but an intentional restart can look similar.
AnomalyRapidCollapseDetail: Charge fell by about {value} percentage points within roughly 30 minutes. This is consistent with a severe gauge/cutoff symptom and should be confirmed with Collapse Watch; it does not identify a specific failed cell.
FirmwareRecalibrationDetected: Large firmware/BMS capacity re-estimation detected after restart
VoltageSagScoreHint: Higher score means more severe or repeated short-term voltage sag. This is an observation score, not a cell-level diagnosis.
ReliabilityScoreHint: Reliability combines capacity, gauge behavior, voltage sag, and collapse evidence. It is a heuristic screening score.
FirmwareRecalibrationHint: A large change in full-charge capacity immediately after a collapse can indicate that the battery controller re-estimated usable capacity.
HealthFirmwareReestimated: Current firmware/BMS capacity estimate. A large re-estimation was detected after the recovered shutdown, so this value may have changed abruptly.
CollapseExportNotYet: Recovered-collapse report has not been exported yet.
DiagnosticSummaryDetail: Separates capacity, gauge accuracy, voltage stability, and shutdown reliability so a single health percentage does not hide sudden-cutoff problems.
PercentageUnreliable: Battery percentage is currently not reliable for predicting remaining runtime. A sudden cutoff occurred while substantial charge was still reported.
PercentageQuestionable: Battery percentage may be unreliable. Confirm with Collapse Watch before relying on it for remaining runtime.
PercentageNoIssueDetected: No strong gauge-reliability issue has been recovered from a shutdown session.
RecommendationCriticalTitle: Plan battery replacement and do not rely on the displayed percentage
RecommendationCriticalDetail: A sudden power cutoff was recovered while Windows still reported substantial charge, with severe voltage sag and/or a major gauge jump. Keep the charger available, save work frequently, and plan battery replacement or service. If the battery is swollen, unusually hot, smells abnormal, or the case is deforming, stop using the battery and have the laptop serviced.
RecommendationWarningTitle: Treat the battery percentage cautiously and continue controlled testing
RecommendationWarningDetail: The available evidence suggests unstable voltage, gauge behavior, or an interrupted discharge session. Avoid depending on the displayed percentage for critical work until a longer controlled test confirms the behavior.
RecommendationReplaceTitle: Capacity is very low; consider replacement based on runtime needs
RecommendationReplaceDetail: The current firmware capacity estimate is heavily degraded. If practical runtime is no longer sufficient, battery replacement is reasonable even if no sudden-cutoff evidence has been recorded.
RecommendationMonitorDetail: No critical collapse evidence is currently available. Continue normal monitoring and repeat a controlled test if runtime or percentage behavior changes.
CollapseReportDisclaimer: Battery Doctor uses values reported by Windows/firmware plus observed discharge behavior. Reliability scores are heuristic screening indicators and cannot identify an individual failed cell. Observed energy from a partial session is not a laboratory full-capacity measurement.
BackgroundMonitoringHint: Battery Doctor can keep watching battery behavior while the window is minimized to the system tray. Monitoring remains local to this PC.
EnableBackgroundMonitoring: Monitor battery while hidden in the tray
EnableTrayNotifications: Show tray alerts for critical battery behavior
StartupPrivacyHint: Startup uses the current-user Windows Run key. No account, cloud service, or telemetry is required.
BackgroundMonitoringOff: Background monitoring is disabled when the window is hidden
NoBackgroundAlertDetail: Battery Doctor has not raised a critical background alert in this session.
AboutDescription: Free, offline-first battery diagnostics for Windows. Battery Doctor combines reported capacity, live discharge behavior, voltage sag, gauge reliability, and sudden-cutoff recovery evidence.
LinkNotConfigured: Project link is not configured yet in AppLinks.json.
SupportLinkNotConfigured: Support link is not configured yet. Set SupportUrl in AppLinks.json before public release.
DonationNoUnlock: Support is optional and does not unlock features. Battery Doctor remains free to use.
PrivacyDetail: Battery analysis, history, settings, and collapse journals stay on this PC. Battery Doctor does not require a server or account for diagnostics.
TrayMinimizedDetail: The window is hidden in the system tray. Background monitoring continues while enabled.
AlertReliabilityCriticalDetail: A previous sudden-cutoff session rated battery reliability at {score}/100. Keep the charger nearby and save work frequently.
AlertBatteryCriticalTitle: Windows reports a critical battery state
AlertBatteryCriticalDetail: Save your work and connect the charger. The battery subsystem is reporting a critical state.
AlertVoltageSagDetail: Voltage dropped about {sag} V over a short interval while the battery reported {charge}. Save work and connect the charger if available.
AlertGaugeJumpTitle: Battery percentage is dropping abnormally fast
AlertGaugeJumpDetail: Battery Doctor observed an abnormal drop of about {value} percentage points. The displayed battery percentage may be unreliable.
StartupSettingFailed: Could not update Windows startup setting
SettingsSaveFailed: Could not save Battery Doctor settings
TestNotificationDetail: Tray notifications are working. This is only a test and does not indicate a battery fault.
TemperatureUnavailableHint: The battery/firmware does not expose a battery temperature sensor to Windows.
EstimatedCurrentHint: Derived from pack power ÷ pack voltage; not a direct current sensor reading.
DynamicResistanceHint: Estimated from short load steps using ΔV/ΔI. Treat as a trend indicator, not laboratory impedance.
CorrelationHint: Descriptive Pearson correlation only; battery temperature can lag electrical load.
TemperatureTrendHint: Uses only a temperature reported by the battery stack. CPU/GPU/ACPI thermal-zone values are never substituted.
CurrentTrendHint: Positive means charging; negative means discharging. Estimated from power and voltage.
